title: Tenant-priority pump-and-drain chaos to validate circuit suppression and graceful shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: validate that tenant-priority throttles and circuit-breaker suppression prevent cascading failures during coordinated GPU pool exhaustion and region ejection. This experiment (pump-and-drain) will artificially inflate request pressure for a small set of tenants while progressively draining GPU capacity in one region and simultaneously introducing dependency blackholes for a downstream storage tier.
description_details: Scope: staging and pre-production canaries only. Target two regions (us-east-1-primary, us-east-1-secondary) and 3 tenant profiles: HighPriority (internal infra), Standard (regular customers), Background (batch jobs). We will exercise: (1) per-tenant admission controls and priority-based shedding; (2) circuit-breaker opening times for dependent services; (3) failover routing to secondary region and the interaction with request throttles; (4) cache behavior and KV prefix reclamation under starved KV capacity.
hypothesis: If tenant-priority admission + adaptive circuit suppression are configured correctly, then during GPU starvation and dependency blackholes: high-priority requests maintain SLOs (p99 latency <= 450ms, error rate < 1%), standard tenants see graceful degradation (increased latency and shaped error rates), and background tenants are heavily shed without causing downstream circuit storms or region-wide overload.
acceptance_criteria: HighPriority tenants maintain p99 latency <= 450ms and error rate < 1% during peak drain window
No circuit-open events cascade across regions (max cross-region circuit propagation rate < 5%)
System automatically routes >=90% of eligible Standard traffic to secondary region within configured failover window when primary is degraded
Background tenants experience >=70% shedding and do not cause control-plane alerts beyond expected thresholds
Runbook rollback is validated end-to-end with automatic un-drain and capacity reclamation within 10 minutes
steps: 1) Pre-checks: snapshot current staging capacity; ensure canary token sets are ready; notify oncall and stakeholders; open monitoring window
2) Baseline: 15m normal load capture for all metrics, per-tenant SLO baseline
3) Pump: gradually ramp synthetic traffic for HighPriority and Standard tenants to target QPS (HighPriority = +50% baseline, Standard = +200%), observe autoscaler behavior
4) Drain: trigger controlled GPU pod eviction sequence in primary region to reduce available GPUs by 60% over 6 minutes (use graceful drain where possible)
5) Blackhole: while drain is progressing, inject dependency blackhole on storage tier for 50% of Standard requests for 3 minutes to force upstream retries and circuit evaluations
6) Observe: monitor circuit-opened_count, failover_routing_rate, throttled_requests_count, and latency/error metrics in real time
7) Tune window: if circuit storm or unexpected control-plane pressure occurs, hit abort and run emergency rollback (un-drain, scale up, re-enable dependency)
8) Recovery: remove blackholes, restore GPU capacity, capture 30m post-run metrics, and run sanity traffic for 10m
9) Analysis: compare baseline vs run, annotate dashboard, propose parameter changes (circuit thresholds, shed percentages, priority weights)
10) Follow-ups: implement tuned settings in staging and re-run; plan gradual rollout to production with canary percentage <> 5% then 25%
observed_results: 2026-03-05 staging dry-run: pump-only run showed HighPriority maintained p99 ~ 430ms, Standard p99 spiked to 1.2s; autoscaler reacted by adding 2 nodes within 90s; no circuit opens observed

2026-03-10 controlled drain dry-run (no blackhole): partial GPU eviction led to queue growth for background tenants; background shed kicked in at ~65% capacity as configured; observed increased request latencies but no cross-region failover triggered (expected)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: control-plane ejection if scheduler misinterprets mass-eviction -> Mitigation: run with control-plane isolation flag and reduce eviction rate
Risk: downstream retry storms causing dependency overload -> Mitigation: enable strict client-side backoff and short-circuiting thresholds before experiment
Risk: noisy neighbor effect for Standard tenants -> Mitigation: cap pump QPS and use tenant quotas; abort if error rate > 5% for HighPriority
rollout_plan: staging: full scenario runs in isolated staging cluster (this ticket)
preprod: reduced blast radius with 5% production-like traffic week-of signoff
prod: phased canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with monitoring gates between stages
postmortem_plan: If any acceptance criteria fail, create a follow-up ticket with root cause analysis and corrective action
Capture timeline and raw metrics to S3, link to this ticket, and schedule a 1-hour blameless review with oncall and SRE
